# 1 Clement Chapter 34 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Alexandrinus, 1 Clement 34 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/1CL_034_page_001.jpg

---

## Chapter 34

**34:1** The good laborer receives the bread of his work with boldness; the lazy and negligent one cannot look his employer in the face.

**34:2** It is therefore necessary that we should be zealous in well-doing; for from him are all things.

**34:3** For he forewarns us: "Behold, the Lord, and his reward is before his face, to render to each according to his work."

**34:4** He therefore exhorts us who believe in him with our whole heart not to be lazy and negligent in every good work.

**34:5** Let our boast and our confidence be in him; let us submit ourselves to his will; let us consider the whole multitude of his angels, how they stand by and minister to his will.

**34:6** For the scripture says: "Ten thousands of ten thousands stood by him, and thousands of thousands ministered to him, and they cried out: Holy, Holy, Holy is the Lord of Sabaoth; the whole of creation is full of his glory."

**34:7** And so let us, being gathered together in harmony in our conscience, cry out to him earnestly as with one voice, that we may become sharers in his great and glorious promises.

**34:8** For it says: "Eye has not seen, and ear has not heard, and it has not entered into the heart of man, what things God has prepared for those who wait for him."

---

*EMET renders with maximal literalness. The Trisagion (v. 6) from Isaiah 6:3 is the earliest recorded Christian use of this text in a liturgical context. The citation in v. 8 is Isaiah 64:4 LXX (also Paul, 1 Cor 2:9).*
